articles.title: How 10,000 Years of Potato Farming Reshaped Human DNA in the Andes
articles.excerpt: A landmark genetic study reveals that Indigenous Andeans carry the world's highest number of starch-digestion genes — an evolutionary adaptation driven by thousands of years of potato cultivation.
articles.image_caption: Freshly harvested potatoes, a staple crop first domesticated in the Andean highlands between 6,000 and 10,000 years ago. A new genetic study links millennia of potato farming to evolutionary changes in human starch digestion.
articles.nri_angle: The research highlights how ancestral diets shape genetic traits, raising questions relevant to diaspora communities whose modern diets may differ significantly from those their genes evolved to process.

articles.title: From Mutton Biryani to Fish Curry: Indian Temples Where Non-Vegetarian Prasad Is Sacred

articles.nri_angle: These non-vegetarian temple traditions highlight the diversity of Hindu practice often unseen in diaspora communities, where temple food tends toward the vegetarian mainstream.
